newsitem.title: USA: Bonds hit near 7 percent amid fears of Fed tightening.
newsitem.headline: Bonds hit near 7 percent amid fears of Fed tightening.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks reversed course to end higher Monday but investors remained worried that the Federal Reserve would boost interest rates next week.
Bond yields rose near the key 7 percent level, the dollar ended mixed and oil and gold fell.
The revamped Dow Jones industrial average rose 20.02 points to 6,955.48 after recovering from a loss of more than 80 points.
But the broader market was mostly lower. Declining issues beat advances by 1,626 to 843 on volume of 494 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
Monday's trading marked the debut of four new components in the 30-stock Dow, as the world's most closely watched stock index became less smokestack- and more technology-oriented.

Added to the list were computer maker Hewlett-Packard, drug maker Johnson & Johnson, Wal-Mart Stores Inc. and insurance company Travelers Group Inc. Dropped were Bethlehem Steel, Westinghouse Electric, Texaco and Woolworth Corp.

The Nasdaq composite index, laced with technology stocks, fell 13.54 points, or 1.05 percent, to 1,279.43. Among leading high-tech names, Intel Corp. shed 1-1/2 to 136-3/8 and International Business Machines fell 4-1/8 to 139-1/2.
The weakness in the broader market underscored how eager investors were to take profits before the March 25 meeting of Fed policy-makers, analysts said.
High tech stocks "have lost momentum and nobody's willing to step up here," said Guy Truicko, equity portfolio manager at Unity Management. "All eyes are on next week's Fed meeting."
Indeed, investors were gripped by nervousness about interest rates, as Wall Street sensed that the odds favoured a rise in short-term rates by the central bank to ward off inflation.
In the bond market, the benchmark 30-year Treasury fell 6/32, raising its yield to 6.96 percent from 6.94 percent at Friday's close. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.

In a sign of stocks' sensitivity to interest rates, the Dow index rebounded sharply in late trading when the 30-year Treasury bond rebounded after briefly hitting the psychologically important 7 percent level. Long-term bond yields of 7 percent tend to draw funds from stocks to bonds.
The dollar fell against the mark as investors flocked to the German currency on news that British Prime Minister John Major was calling a general election.
The dollar rose against the weakened pound and edged higher against the Japanese yen.

The dollar stood at 1.6910 marks in late New York trading, down from 1.6950 marks at Friday's close. The dollar edged up to 123.74 yen from 123.50 late on Friday. The British pound slid to $1.5887 from $1.6013.
In commodities markets, coffee prices fell sharply as worries about tight supplies eased with reports of rising stocks at coffee warehouses.

Coffee for May delivery fell 17.70 cents to 168.65 cents a pound at the Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange. It was the biggest one-day drop since the current rally began in December and the lowest closing price in three weeks.
Oil prices closed lower, with April crude off 37 cents at $20.92 a barrel at the New York Mercantile Exchange.
April gold lost $4.70 to $348.30 an ounce at New York's Commodity Exchange.
Overseas, London's FTSE 100 index lost 51 points to 4,373.3 and Tokyo's Nikkei 225 stock index rose 129.86 points to 18,053.50.
